headwords: chó cứ sủa còn đoàn người cứ đi

flags.why: The bird or chick sound is the meaning learners are more likely to encounter ([dictionary](https://loigiaihay.com/tu-dien-tv/chiu-chit-edegm5tdxYBsa.html)).
This is a current, ordinary breed name, so the rare tag is misleading ([Pedigree Vietnam](https://www.pedigree.com.vn/cac-giong-cho/cho-chan-duc)).
The example defines the breed instead of showing the word in use.
flags.fix: Nhà tôi nuôi một con chó lài. = My family keeps an Indochinese dingo.

flags.why: Chó xù describes a shaggy or fluffy-haired dog rather than specifically identifying a bichon ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-x%C3%B9)).
flags.fix: Gloss: shaggy-haired dog; fluffy-haired dog. Example translation: We have a white fluffy-haired dog.

flags.why: Chó đểu is an insult directed at someone, not a general exclamation meaning damn it ([dictionary](https://vdict.com/ch%C3%B3%20%C4%91%E1%BB%83u%2C2%2C0%2C0.html)).
The example explains the slang expression instead of using it to refer to HIV.
flags.fix: Nó sợ mình dính chôm chôm. = He's afraid he's contracted HIV.

flags.why: Chõng remains a current word for this furniture, so dated misleadingly describes the word as outdated ([current usage](https://thegioibanghe.vn/bo-ban-ghe-chong-tre/)).
